core_obligations: Start from a monic polynomial f over A and a factorisation of its reduction modulo I into monic coprime factors g_0 and h_0, and let e be the idempotent of A/I[T]/(f) corresponding to (1, 0) (proof lines 3630-3638).
Write f as a product of linear factors with roots a_i in A, evaluate e at each root to obtain idempotents e_i of A/I, and lift them to idempotents of A using hypothesis (2) (proof lines 3638-3644).
Decompose A as a finite product of rings in which each e_i is 0 or 1, which reduces the problem to the case handled in the next step (proof lines 3643-3647).

Assume e_i = 1 for i up to r and 0 afterwards, use the Bezout relation between g_0 and h_0 to see that h_0(a_i) is a unit for i at most r, deduce that T - a_1 divides g_0 in A/I[T], and lift the factorisation of the remaining product inductively on the degree (proof lines 3650-3669).

difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a sufficient condition for an ideal in an absolutely integrally closed ring to define a henselian pair: the ideal must lie in the Jacobson radical and the quotient map must induce a bijection on idempotents (statement lines 3619-3627). The proof is the longest of this batch at 41 lines (proof lines 3630-3670) and it is a real construction: from a factorisation of a monic polynomial modulo I into two monic factors generating the unit ideal, it produces the idempotent of the quotient A/I[T]/(f) corresponding to (1, 0), writes f as a product of linear factors with roots a_i in A using absolute integral closedness, evaluates the idempotent at each root to get idempotents e_i of A/I, lifts them to idempotents of A by the hypothesis on idempotents, decomposes A as a finite product of rings in which each e_i is 0 or 1, and then lifts the factorisation inductively using the fact that one factor becomes a unit at the roots in question. The decomposition into a product of rings is stated with the author's own note that some details are omitted, and the induction on the degree is carried out in full.
